successCriteria.description: A new employee routes module exists that registers a profile endpoint which resolves the authenticated actor from `request.user` (rejecting a missing/invalid actor with UnauthorizedError) and returns the result of `employeeService.getEmployeeProfileById(actor.id)` with HTTP 200.
The profile response never contains `passwordHash` (nor `terminationDate`) — the returned object is the `EmployeeProfile` shape from `src/shared/types`, not the raw `Employee`.
`src/modules/employee/index.ts` re-exports `employeeRoutes` so it is importable through the module's public entry point.
`src/app.ts` registers `employeeRoutes` (after `registerAuth` so the auth preHandler populates `request.user`), making the endpoint reachable at runtime.

constraints: No controller file — the route handler calls `employeeService.getEmployeeProfileById` directly, matching the codebase's universal routes-call-services shape (binding rule 1).

The route must reuse the `resolveActor`/`sendError` shape from `src/modules/leave/leave.routes.ts` (actor resolved from `request.user`, role membership enforced at the API boundary; `AppError` → `{ error, code }` with its status, any other throw → 500). Local copies are acceptable per the balance/auth precedent; the shape must be identical.

Read-only endpoint: no transaction, no writes, no audit record, no repository access in the route — the route only resolves the actor and delegates to the existing `getEmployeeProfileById` service method.
The service instance is resolved from `fastify.employeeService` if present, else a factory-constructed default (mirroring `createLeaveService`/`createBalanceService`), so tests can inject a fake.
outOfScope: Unit tests for auth service and leave routes (`tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.routes.test.ts`, `tests/unit/modules/auth/auth.service.test.ts`) — Sub-phase 7.3. This sub-phase must not create test files or gate on test coverage.
Any change to `getEmployeeProfileById`/`toEmployeeProfile` in `employee.service.ts` or to the `EmployeeProfile` type — those are Phase 2 deliverables treated as fixed contracts.

entityInvariants.invariant: The profile returned by the endpoint is the `EmployeeProfile` shape from `src/shared/types` — it never carries `passwordHash` or `terminationDate`, regardless of the underlying `Employee` row.
The endpoint is read-only: it never mutates the `Employee` entity, its `passwordHash`, or any other persisted field.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: The caller's identity is resolved from the verified token (`request.user`), never a client-supplied id; the route passes `actor.id`.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Unknown employee id → NotFoundError (404); missing/invalid actor → UnauthorizedError (401); any other throw → 500.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Reuse the `resolveActor`/`sendError` helper shape exactly as implemented in the leave routes (actor from `request.user`, role membership check, `AppError` → `{ error, code }` with status, else 500).
Call the existing `IEmployeeService.getEmployeeProfileById` (which already maps via `toEmployeeProfile` and omits `passwordHash`/`terminationDate`) — do not re-implement profile mapping in the route.
Return the `EmployeeProfile` type declared in shared types (no `passwordHash`, no `terminationDate`).
Register the route after `registerAuth` so the auth preHandler populates `request.user` before the handler runs.

integrationPoints.why: The route delegates profile resolution to this existing Phase 2 method; it is the single source of the passwordHash/terminationDate omission.
Populates `request.user` from the verified JWT so `resolveActor` can resolve the actor; the route must be registered after this hook.
The route's actor resolution and error mapping depend on these typed errors for the 401/404/500 semantics.
